title: Index of Core Industries: combined index
description: Monthly index of the combined index of all core industries, part of the Index of Core Industries compiled by the Office of the Economic Adviser (DPIIT). Base 2022-23=100 (from the June 2026 release; weight 100). The previous 2011-12=100 series (eight industries, March 2019 to May 2026, discontinued) is kept as separate views and is not chained to the new one. Published provisionally about 20 days after month end. The combined index moves with industrial and infrastructure activity and arrives about three weeks after the month end, well before quarterly GDP data.
source: PIB / Office of the Economic Adviser, DPIIT

qna.question: What is this core industry index (combined)?
qna.answer: The Index of Core Industries (ICI) measures physical production volumes in the core industries: coal, crude oil, natural gas, refinery products, fertilizers, steel, cement, electricity and (new in the 2022-23 series) iron ore. This indicator is the combined index of all core industries.^Following the earlier practice, the ICI weights are derived from the weights of the corresponding items of the IIP.

qna.question: How should I read it?
qna.answer: Index levels compare a month with the 2022-23 average (=100). Production is seasonal, so use the year-on-year growth view for momentum, and treat the latest month as provisional.^The combined index moves with industrial and infrastructure activity and arrives about three weeks after the month end, well before quarterly GDP data. Year-on-year growth is the figure PIB publishes (one decimal).

qna.question: Base year, revisions and caveats
qna.answer: From the June 2026 release the OEA publishes the ICI on base 2022-23=100 and has discontinued the 2011-12 series (its linking factor for the combined index between the two is 1.47). The 2022-23 series differs in coverage: iron ore added, gross steel production, raw coal only. Old and new levels are not comparable, so they are separate views.^Months are provisional at first release and revised in the following month's release. The figures here come from PIB press releases, whose tables carry the last 13 months, so the new-base history on this page starts in June 2025; the OEA back series from April 2023 is hosted on a website with a broken TLS certificate and is not used.

note: History on the 2022-23 base begins June 2025 (13-month tables in PIB releases).
